presentation.title_rationale: The selected title leads with the reader's own question and then names both terms the page actually budgets - VRAM (weights plus overhead) and KV cache - so the promise is one supported benefit: you can decide fit before loading. It drops the previous 91-character subtitle, the year label and the methods clause ('math behind the context you can actually serve'), and asserts no speed, saving or benchmark number; the body supplies the per-model table and the hybrid-attention counterexample that back the question's answer.
presentation.visual_purpose: The cover is a three-step checklist for the page's budget identity: model configuration (weights, from the model's own config and published GGUF size), context plus concurrency (the KV cache slope and per-slot multiplier), and available memory (the device capacity the total is compared against). Its caption tells the reader to state the assumptions before comparing totals, matching the body's declared rather than measured 1 GiB overhead. It carries no numbers or measured values and is explicitly labelled a conceptual checklist.
